sector.narrative: 1.1 By 2030, eradicate extreme poverty for all people everywhere, currently measured as people living on less than $1.25 a day

8.3 Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, and encourage the formalization and growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, including through access to financial services
8.5 By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value
Output 2.2. Increased capacity of Member States to apply international labour standards
Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis
Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

tag.narrative: This activity is implemented partially in response to the COVID-19 pandemic

title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
The Federal Government of Somalia, in consultation with the social partners, implemented a programme on rehabilitation and repair of basic infrastructure using pro-employment approaches to promote employment and decent work measures to tackle fragility drivers in conflict or disaster settings, considering the humanitarian-development-peace nexus. This has resulted in community resilience and peace building through rehabilitation and repair of basic infrastructure using pro-employment approaches. Furthermore, local contracting industry strengthened through promoting employment-intensive approach and the development of emerging entrepreneurs with the aim of increasing their participation in the delivery of public infrastructure.
These results have been documented in progress reports of the Somalia Joint Programme on Local Governance and Decentralized Service Delivery, UN-JPLG (Phase III) and the project on Sustainable return and reintegration through Employment-Intensive Infrastructure works. Reports can be accessed following the links provided under the section on “Source of information”. ILO provide technical assistance to Public works technical staff of thirty (30) local government districts have been capacitated to plan, design, implement and monitor inclusive and labor-intensive infrastructure investment with decent work principles to reintegrate Internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees into communities. Procedure for the recruitment of beneficiaries developed in consultation with key partners. Special attention given to vulnerable members of communities. ILO is supporting to enhance competencies, capacities, systems and structures for the delivery of infrastructure service; promoting the adoption and institutionalization of labour-based technologies at the local government level. 30 local government institutions have been capacitated from 2022 to date. A total of ten (10) capacity building workshops have been implemented and attended by a total of 261 persons from Government institutions, civil society, community leaders, contractors, workers and community members.
The local governments in Somalia with technical support from the ILO now use employment intensive approaches in infrastructure investment to provide immediate employment opportunities for IDPs, returnees and the host communities. On-the job skills training also allow beneficiaries to access new income-generating opportunities in construction related activities. These activities have facilitated communication and interaction as well as provide information on socio-economic activities. A total of 284,385 worker-days of employment have been created from the rehabilitation of 42 community assets. 8 villages committees have been established in the IDPs hosting community to oversee the operation and maintenance of rehabilitated assets.

title.narrative: 3.4.1. Number of Member States with programmes to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work
Output 2.2. Increased capacity of Member States to apply international labour standards

description.narrative: The tripartite constituents of Somalia validated and adopted the Country’s Decent Work Programme (2023-2025). The Decent Work Country Programme- DWCP (2023-2025) of Somalia was adopted officially with the signing of the document by the tripartite constituents and the ILO during the ILC held in June 2023 in Geneva. The country priorities and the Country Programme Outcomes (CPOs) in the DWCP 2023-2025 align with the National Development Plan 2021-2025, Pillars 3 and 4. Therefore, the country priorities and CPOs reflect the employment-related agenda the Federal Government of Somalia, its social partners, private sector, and other stakeholders believe necessary to attain peacebuilding, recovery, growth, and development. The DWCP prioritized a backlog of reporting of C029, C087,C098 and the domestication of C097, C143, C144, C155, C181, C187 and C190 during the DWCP period. The development of DWCP 2023-2025 was initiated with the technical support of ILO in September 2019 with the preparation of a country diagnostic assessment. The country diagnostic provided an evidence-based analysis of the country’s situation covering the social, political and economic context and across each of the four ILO strategic objectives (employment; social protection; social dialogue and tripartism; and fundamental principles and rights at work). The country diagnostic analysis based on secondary sources and consultative interviews with the relevant tripartite stakeholders helped highlight significant work deficits and opportunities to create full and productive employment in Somalia. Based on the Somali context’s identified decent work challenges, a prioritisation exercise was carried out in November 2019 to narrow down to four main priority areas for the DWCP. The partners and stakeholders’ feedback was consolidated, presented, and discussed in a three-day DWCP Consultative Workshop held in Mogadishu from 9th to 11th December 2019. During the Workshop, the tripartite partners, which included representation at federal and state levels inclusive of gender and youth mix, discussed and ranked the four country priorities and Country Programme Outcomes (CPOs) and outputs that form part of the DWCP 2023-2025. A revised list of country priorities and CPOs was developed and adopted based on the consultations and dialogue, including on reporting backlogs.
